title: Xanthe and the Postcards
premise: Juniper Whitlock, a translator whose childhood language is dissolving word by word, returns to her late grandmother's house to settle the estate and discovers a box of undelivered postcards hidden behind a wardrobe — all written by her grandmother to a man Juniper never knew existed. As she translates them, she uncovers how her grandmother survived an occupation-era betrayal that made the family's fortune, and that the man in the photographs, Tomas, was the one who paid its price. When Tomas's grandson arrives demanding answers and the last of the inheritance, Juniper must choose between protecting the family myth and delivering the truth; in the end she mails the final postcard — the one her grandmother never sent — and gives the house away, keeping only the words she can still remember.
about_author: Sebastian Ravensworth is the pen name of a former court interpreter who spent a decade listening to testimony in languages on the verge of extinction. They live near a decommissioned border crossing and write about what families bury in order to continue.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV, catalogues her fading vocabulary in a notebook while packing up her London flat after losing a translation contract. She learns her grandmother Vespera has died and left her the house. Emotional beat: quiet dread disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A House That Outlived Its Language
chapters.summary: Juniper arrives at the decaying family house in the river valley town of Miren. The neighbors speak her disappearing dialect fluently; she can barely order bread. POV Juniper. Beat: alienation in a place that should be home.

chapters.title: Behind the Wardrobe
chapters.summary: Clearing the bedroom, Juniper finds a loose panel and a tin box: forty-one undelivered postcards, all addressed to 'Tomas Verel,' spanning 1943–1946, in her grandmother's hand. POV Juniper. Beat: vertigo — the past has been waiting.

chapters.title: The First Card
chapters.summary: Juniper translates the earliest postcard, dated during the occupation, and realizes the coded phrases reference something hidden. Her dialect fails her; she must ask the neighbor Ilse for help. POV Juniper. Beat: reluctant dependence.

chapters.title: Ilse Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Ilse, ninety, offers fragments: Vespera was 'the one who stayed' while others fled or vanished. She warns Juniper not to dig. POV shifts partly to Ilse's oral account. Beat: first crack in the family legend.

chapters.title: What the Photographs Kept
chapters.summary: Among the estate papers Juniper finds photos of young Vespera with a man — Tomas — laughing in front of the very wardrobe. Her mother had told her Vespera came to Miren alone. POV Juniper. Beat: grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Word for Betrayal
chapters.summary: Translating card seven, Juniper hits a word with no modern equivalent — a term meaning both 'to save' and 'to sell.' She begins a glossary of lost terms. POV Juniper. Beat: language as evidence.

chapters.title: A Letter from a Stranger
chapters.summary: A lawyer's letter arrives: a Daniel Verel contests the estate, claiming his grandfather held title to half the property. Juniper realizes Tomas's family never stopped waiting. POV Juniper. Beat: the past acquires legal teeth.

chapters.title: Daniel Arrives
chapters.summary: Daniel Verel, blunt and grieving his own father, shows up at the gate with his grandfather's diary. He and Juniper circle each other, each holding half a story. POV alternates Juniper/Daniel. Beat: wary collision.

chapters.title: Two Diaries, One Summer
chapters.summary: Comparing texts, they reconstruct 1943: Vespera and Tomas were engaged before the occupation split the town into collaborators, resisters, and survivors. POV dual via documents. Beat: intimacy across generations.

chapters.title: Card Nineteen: The Bridge
chapters.summary: A postcard describes a night meeting at the rail bridge — the same bridge where, town records say, a shipment disappeared. Juniper begins to suspect Vespera informed on someone. POV Juniper. Beat: dread sharpening.

chapters.title: The Fortune in the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Ilse reveals the Whitlock money came from goods 'recovered' after deportations — including from the Verel family. Juniper confronts the price of her own existence. POV Juniper. Beat: inheritance as wound.

chapters.title: Daniel's Anger
chapters.summary: Daniel, having read further in the diary, accuses Vespera of betraying Tomas to save herself. Juniper defends her grandmother without believing it. POV Daniel-led. Beat: rage as grief's twin.

chapters.title: The Untranslatable Year
chapters.summary: Juniper's glossary grows; she notices her dreams have begun arriving fully in the old dialect — memory returning as the language does. POV Juniper. Beat: eerie reclamation.

chapters.title: Card Thirty-Three: Forgiveness Drafted
chapters.summary: Late cards shift tone: Vespera asking Tomas's forgiveness in increasingly desperate terms, never sent. Why did she stop sending? POV Juniper. Beat: pity displacing judgment.

chapters.title: The Town's Version
chapters.summary: At Ilse's urging, Juniper attends a memorial gathering where the town's official story — Vespera as quiet heroine — is recited. She says nothing. POV Juniper. Beat: complicity recognized.

chapters.title: The Missing Fortieth
chapters.summary: There are forty-one cards but the numbering skips none except a gap in dates: three months unaccounted for in winter 1944. Something happened that produced no writing at all. POV Juniper. Beat: the shape of silence.

chapters.title: Archives and Ash
chapters.summary: Juniper travels to the regional archive; most occupation files burned, but a transport ledger survives listing names — including Tomas Verel, marked 'released' through intervention by 'V.W.' POV Juniper. Beat: reversal — Vespera saved him?

chapters.title: Then Who Did She Betray?
chapters.summary: If Vespera saved Tomas, someone else was traded. Cross-referencing, Juniper finds a second name on the ledger: her own great-aunt, Liora, deported in Tomas's place. POV Juniper. Beat: horror of arithmetic.

chapters.title: Liora
chapters.summary: Juniper researches Liora Whitlock, erased from every family story, and finds a survivor's testimony mentioning her last words. Juniper's mother had said Liora 'went abroad.' POV Juniper. Beat: the erasure named.

chapters.title: Confronting Ilse
chapters.summary: Juniper demands the truth; Ilse admits the town knew and chose Vespera's version because condemning her meant condemning everyone who bought the recovered goods. POV Ilse-heavy. Beat: collective guilt surfaces.

chapters.title: Daniel Reads the Last Diary Page
chapters.summary: Tomas's diary ends mid-sentence in 1945. Daniel confesses his grandfather never spoke again after the war — the silence inherited like property. POV Daniel. Beat: two silences recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Daniel proposes a settlement: he'll drop the claim if Juniper publicly acknowledges the house's origin. Juniper hesitates — exposure would destroy her dying mother's peace. POV Juniper. Beat: survival's price, again.

chapters.title: Mother on the Line
chapters.summary: Juniper calls her mother, who admits she always knew about Liora and chose the myth to protect Juniper's childhood. The call ends badly. POV Juniper. Beat: generational bargain exposed.

chapters.title: Winter Comes Early
chapters.summary: Snow isolates the house; Juniper, feverish, rereads all forty-one cards in order and finally understands their sequence is a confession structured as love letters. POV Juniper. Beat: pattern revealed.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Night
chapters.summary: Juniper walks to the rail bridge in snow and reconstructs the 1944 meeting: Vespera was given a choice — one name. She gave Liora's to free Tomas, then could never send another word to him. POV Juniper. Beat: climax of understanding.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Juniper drafts a public statement naming Liora and the fortune's source, and destroys nothing this time — no burning, no hiding. POV Juniper. Beat: breaking the inheritance of silence.

chapters.title: Daniel at the Door Again
chapters.summary: Before Juniper can publish, Daniel arrives having found Liora's name himself; his fury breaks into shared mourning rather than demand. POV Daniel. Beat: enemy becomes witness.

chapters.title: The Town Reacts
chapters.summary: The statement circulates; some neighbors thank Juniper, others cut her dead. Ilse, dying, asks to see her. POV Juniper. Beat: truth's mixed harvest.

chapters.title: Ilse's Confession
chapters.summary: Ilse reveals she was the one who told the occupiers where Liora hid — Vespera took the blame to shield Ilse, whose family fed the town through the war. POV Ilse. Beat: guilt redistributed, not absolved.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Cards
chapters.summary: Juniper realizes the unsent cards weren't cowardice but penance: Vespera wrote to Tomas yearly because speaking would have ended the debt. POV Juniper. Beat: compassion without excuse.

chapters.title: The Final Postcard
chapters.summary: In the tin's false bottom Juniper finds card forty-two, blank except for Liora's name — Vespera's unfinished apology. Juniper decides to finish and send it. POV Juniper. Beat: completing the dead's sentence.

chapters.title: Mailing It
chapters.summary: Juniper addresses the card to the Verel family plot in the relocated cemetery and mails it — postage for a letter sixty years late. POV Juniper. Beat: ritual accomplished.

chapters.title: Deed of Gift
chapters.summary: Juniper signs the house over jointly: half to Daniel, half to the town as a memorial reading room for Liora and the deported. POV Juniper. Beat: inheritance redirected.

chapters.title: Mother Comes Home
chapters.summary: Juniper's mother visits, sees the memorial plaque, and for the first time speaks Liora's name aloud in the old dialect. Reconciliation, incomplete but real. POV alternating. Beat: thaw.

chapters.title: The Glossary Published
chapters.summary: Juniper publishes her glossary of untranslatable words — including the word meaning both 'to save' and 'to sell' — dedicated to Liora. POV Juniper. Beat: language restored as testimony.

chapters.title: Last Words Remembered
chapters.summary: Juniper translates the survivor's testimony line about Liora's final words and adds it to the memorial wall. The dialect comes back to her fully in dreams now. POV Juniper. Beat: mourning completed.

chapters.title: Leaving Miren
chapters.summary: Juniper packs to leave, keeping only the notebook and one photograph — Vespera and Tomas, faces turned toward whoever stood behind the camera. POV Juniper. Beat: lightness after reckoning.

chapters.title: Postmark
chapters.summary: Weeks later, a reply arrives forwarded from Miren: a Verel descendant writes that the card was read aloud at the grave. The debt is acknowledged, not erased. POV Juniper. Beat: grace, partial.

chapters.title: The Word I Keep
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Juniper, translating again in London, teaches her niece one old word each visit — beginning with the one that means both saving and selling, so the price is never forgotten. POV Juniper. Beat: inheritance chosen, not imposed.
